subject: Request: burst capacity & SLA guarantee for Apr 5 go-live
messages:
From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@cloudmed.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudMed Platform Ops <ops@cloudmed.io>
Date: 2026-03-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: burst capacity & SLA guarantee for Apr 5 go-live

Hi Sean,

We're finalizing the production cutover for CloudMed on Apr 5 and expect a concentrated traffic spike during the first 2 hours after go-live (estimated baseline 100 rps -> peak ~380 rps). Our SREs are asking whether Redwood can provide a temporary burst capacity guarantee and a short SLA commitment for that window to avoid automatic throttling/fairness-based degradation.

Specifically: any chance Redwood can provide a temporary quota override to allow up to 400 rps for a 2 hour window (Apr 5, 09:00–11:00 PT) and commit to latency SLOs at p95 < 200ms for that window, with an operational contact and runbook? We can sign an addendum and cover incremental usage.

Attaching our capacity plan and traffic profile. Let me know what information you need.

Thanks,
Alice Tan
Platform Ops — CloudMed Inc
attachments: cloudmed_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@cloudmed.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: burst capacity & SLA guarantee for Apr 5 go-live

Hi Alice — thanks for the details and attachment.

We can support temporary increases, but I need to confirm a couple of operational constraints and routing policies with our capacity and legal teams:
- Which API endpoints will see the spike (generation vs embeddings vs streaming)?
- Exact expected token rate vs request rate (sheet helps but explicit rps/p50/p95 numbers are helpful).
- Will you need burst for a single API key or multiple tenants?

I'll escalate and propose a concrete temporary quota override + monitoring plan. CCing Lauren and Aditya to confirm approval path and billing addendum. I'll aim to send a formal proposal by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-26T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: CloudMed burst request — proposed terms

Lauren / Aditya,

Context: CloudMed requests a temporary quota override for Apr 5 go-live. Baseline traffic ~100 rps; target peak ~380 rps for ~2 hours. They will sign an addendum and cover incremental usage.

My proposed operational terms (draft):
- Temporary override: increase rate limit for the CloudMed production API key to 4x baseline (max 400 rps) for a 2 hour window on 2026-04-05 09:00–11:00 PT.
- Fairness policy exception: suspend automated fairness throttling for the key during the window; other customers still protected by a global soft cap to prevent cluster-wide saturation.
- Latency SLO: Redwood will target p95 latency < 200ms for generation requests routed to the hosted cluster; we will provide a best-effort 99.0% uptime commitment for that 2-hour window (note: hosted multi-tenant environment).
- Pre-warm: we will provision burst capacity and run a 30-minute pre-warm starting 08:30 PT. CloudMed to send low-rate synthetic traffic and standby engineers.
- Monitoring & runbook: on-call from Redwood infra + CloudMed SREs; escalation path and shared Slack channel.
- Billing: incremental usage at overage rate with a one-time credit that we can negotiate (finance approval needed).
- Termination clause: automatic fallback to baseline if sustained degradation or cluster health issues detected; we will notify CloudMed 5 minutes prior to fallback.

Attachments: quota_override_request.pdf (formal override request template).

Questions: do we want to make the latency SLO contractual or an operational target? If contractual, legal will need to sign off on SLA language and remedies/credits. Also need finance to pre-approve a provisional credit band for the addendum.

Recommend: approve temporary override subject to legal addendum and finance sign-off. I'll draft the client-facing email and DocuSign addendum.

Thanks,
Sean
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudMed burst request — proposed terms

+1 to proceeding but with conditions:
- Make latency an operational SLO (target) and keep contractual remedies limited to service credits tied to measurable availability (avoid latency penalty language).
- Finance: offer a 30% usage credit cap on incremental charge (pre-approved by finance but subject to final review).
- Legal: need a short addendum that (a) scopes the window, (b) specifies fallback behavior, and (c) includes a mutual force-majeure carve-out.
- Ops: require that our autoscaling metrics show headroom >15% for 10 minutes before we allow full 4x; otherwise scale to 2x and extend pre-warm.

Please loop in legal/finance and send the draft DocuSign link. Once legal approves wording, we can send to CloudMed.

-Lauren
VP Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@cloudmed.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary burst capacity & SLA addendum (draft) — CloudMed go-live

Hi Alice — thanks for your patience. Per internal approvals, please find our proposed terms below and linked documents. This is intentionally narrow (timeboxed) and requires a signed addendum before we provision the override.

Proposal (summary):
- Window: 2026-04-05 09:00–11:00 PT (pre-warm 08:30–09:00).
- Temporary quota: increase to 400 rps for the CloudMed production API key for the 2-hour window.
- Fairness policy: automated fairness throttling will be suspended for the key during the window; global soft caps remain in effect to prevent cluster-wide saturation.
- Latency: Redwood will operate to a p95 latency target < 200ms for routed generation requests; this is an operational SLO (not a financially-backed SLA).
- Availability SLA: we will provide a 99.0% availability target for the timeboxed window; if availability falls below the target for the window we will issue a service credit in accordance with the addendum.
- Pre-warm & runbook: CloudMed to execute pre-warm synthetic traffic starting 08:30 PT; Redwood will monitor and scale. Shared Slack channel will be created for the window.
- Billing: normal overage rates apply; Redwood will extend a one-time negotiated credit up to 30% of incremental charges (per finance).
- Fallback: automatic rollback to baseline if cluster health falls below safety thresholds; Redwood will provide 5 minutes notice when possible.

Attachments & links: quota_override_request.pdf; cloudmed_sla_addendum_draft.docx; DocuSign draft (https://redwood.docusign.com/CLD-2026-0432-addendum).

Next steps: please review and, if acceptable, sign the DocuSign addendum so we can schedule pre-warm. Happy to hop on a 15m call to walk the runbook.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
attachments: cloudmed_sla_addendum_draft.docx, quota_override_request.pdf
